purpose: Post-hoc LLM coding of blackboard messages; not a replacement for the agent-facing 22-tag list.

specific_tags.definition: Publishing or enforcing a canonical CV split: fold count, seed, row order, class order, and shared fold files.
Saving, naming, validating, or exchanging OOF/test probability arrays, shapes, row order, caches, and artifact indexes.
Preventing leakage between base models, meta-models, folds, and submissions; nested or honest validation of stacking.
TF-IDF, count vectorizers, word/char n-gram construction, vocabulary limits, and sublinear scaling.
Handcrafted text statistics such as length, punctuation, casing, stopword counts, and other stylometric signals.
Per-fold teacher/student self-training, confident test soft labels, and semi-supervised expansion.
Fine-tuning pretrained language models such as BERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTa, XLNet, ELECTRA, ERNIE, MPNet, BART, or DistilBERT.
Training TF-IDF/linear/NB baselines such as LogisticRegression, SVM, NB-SVM, ComplementNB, SGD, or Ridge.
Training gradient-boosted or tree models such as LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, or RandomForest.
Choosing a model family, scale, or pretrained checkpoint for diversity or expected gain.
Fast Gradient Method, AWP, or related embedding-perturbation training used as regularization.
Running the same configuration with multiple random seeds and averaging predictions.
Averaging predictions across epochs or selecting/averaging best checkpoints within a fold.
Tuning learning rate, batch size, epochs, weight decay, or other optimization hyperparameters.
Running or reporting k-fold cross-validation and OOF scores.
Nested CV, fold-wise weight fitting, or explicit control of stacking/selection optimism.
Analyzing error decorrelation and prioritizing genuinely different model families, scales, or feature spaces.
Arithmetic, geometric, rank, or greedy weighted averaging of predictions without a trained meta-learner.
Training a meta-learner on concatenated OOF probabilities or log-probabilities.
Stacking with handcrafted meta-features in addition to base-model probabilities.
Fitting blend or stack weights, including greedy search, constrained optimization, and nested weight selection.
Temperature scaling, probability calibration, or normalization before blending/submission.
Verifying submission ids, row count, class order, probability sums, absence of NaN, and file format.
Per-class errors, confusion patterns, residual analysis, or diagnosis of where the model fails.
A weak model, failed feature family, or negative ablation that should stop or redirect work.
Claiming lanes, proposing a division of labor, or negotiating who does what.
Claiming GPU lanes, posting lock/release signals, and managing compute contention.
Transferring or protecting ownership of final_solution, shared scripts, or submission writes.
Resolving disagreements, write races, duplicated work, or ownership conflicts.
Packaging final code, README, reproduction scripts, and artifact indexes.

role_layer.definition: Owns blending/stacking, combines peer artifacts, and drives the final submission.
Produces diverse base models (transformer, classical, tree) that others can stack.
Develops and transfers training techniques such as FGM, pseudo-labeling, seed averaging, or checkpoint averaging.
Owns fold protocol, nested validation, leakage control, and score integrity.
Coordinates lanes, compute, ownership, deadlines, and handoffs.
Produces error analysis, negative results, and insight that redirect the swarm.
Owns submission validation, final verification, and code release.

rules: Prefer the most specific applicable tag; add the parent base tag only if the message also covers the general category beyond the specific tag.
Use role_* tags only when the message's primary contribution is that role, not merely because the author has that role.
Do not infer tags from the agent identity; use the message content.
Use other only when no tag fits.
For analysis, roll specific tags up to parents; role tags form a separate layer and are not mixed into SI/JSD.
